gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the price per kW of battery-only continuous output across the whole split-phase field. With prices read on 2026-11-10, the order is: Solis 16kW about $285/kW, EG4 FlexBOSS21 about $300/kW, EG4 18kPV $333/kW at Signature Solar's $3,999.99, Sol-Ark 18K about $356–362/kW, Fortress Envy Duo 21 about $408/kW and Sol-Ark 15K about $471/kW.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Eco Solar Kits EG4-vs-Sol-Ark guide, the cited NAZ Solar Electric buying guide and the cited Solar Gear Scout off-grid-vs-hybrid guide, plus the uncited Wildjoule hybrid list. Eco Solar Kits already gives the Sol-Ark 15K's 'about $470 per kW of battery-only output' and calls the FlexBOSS21 the best value per kW. It does not compute the figure for the other models, and it uses $4,898 for the 18kPV, not today's $3,999.99. NAZ gives the Solis 16kW price and its 16 kW battery-only rating but does no per-kW maths, and ChatGPT never named the Solis. Solar Gear Scout ranks by watts per dollar using the headline output, which favours units whose rating needs solar, such as the FlexBOSS21's 16 kW. None of these pages gives idle draw for more than one or two models. Rivals already have part of this finding.
decides: This mostly confirms ChatGPT's 'best value whole-home' pick, the EG4 18kPV. At today's $3,999.99 it costs about $138/kW less than the Sol-Ark 15K for the same 12 kW on battery. The two units that are cheaper per kW each have a named catch. The FlexBOSS21 has a 90 A bypass, so Eco Solar Kits says whole-home installs usually add a GridBOSS or a subpanel. The Solis 16kW weighs 145 lb, the heaviest on NAZ's table. The Sol-Ark 15K's case only holds if its 24 kVA 10-second surge is needed. The 6000XP-class units, including our Sun Gold Power listings, sit in a separate budget off-grid tier: 6–6.5 kW, and the 6000XP has no grid export.
